dimensions.assessment: Directly affects U.S. nationals wrongfully detained or held hostage abroad, their spouses, and dependents.
Provides significant financial and administrative relief by refunding past penalties and suspending tax deadlines during periods of detention.
Involves tax refunds and penalty abatements, but specific aggregate fiscal costs are not stated in the text.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to add specific postponement and refund mechanisms for designated individuals.
Applies permanently to qualifying taxable years ending after enactment, with retroactive refund provisions starting from 2021.

missing_information: Total expected revenue loss or administrative cost to the federal government.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill postpones federal tax deadlines and provides for the refund or abatement of tax penalties, interest, and fines for U.S. nationals who are unlawfully or wrongfully detained or held hostage abroad.

latest_action.text: Passed Senate with an amendment and an amendment to the Title by Unanimous Consent.

card.summary: H.R. 5349, known as the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act or the TAS Act, aims to improve services provided to taxpayers by the Internal Revenue Service by enhancing customer support, updating administrative procedures, and expanding the judicial review powers of the U.S. Tax Court. The bill establishes new technological tools for taxpayers and the IRS, updates rules for tax return preparers, provides protections for specific groups such as taxpayers facing economic hardships or individuals wrongfully detained abroad, and adjusts rules governing the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate and the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.
card.title: TAS Act

card.label: S. 5441

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 670.

card.summary: The Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act (TAS Act) aims to improve taxpayer services provided by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The bill establishes new technological tools for taxpayers and tax professionals, updates IRS procedures regarding collections, appeals, and penalties, modifies rules for tax return preparers and whistleblowers, expands the authority and jurisdiction of the U.S. Tax Court, and provides specific relief for Americans abroad, hostages, and small businesses.
card.title: TAS Act

card.label: H.R. 1
card.summary: H.R. 1 is a sweeping federal budget reconciliation act that adjusts the federal debt limit by $5 trillion and enacts broad changes across multiple sectors. The law modifies safety net and nutrition assistance programs like SNAP and Medicaid, extends and modifies numerous tax provisions and cuts from 2017, alters higher education loans and Pell Grants, scales back or terminates various green energy subsidies while boosting traditional fossil fuel leasing, increases funding for border security, defense, and immigration enforcement, and changes regulations for federal agencies and public lands.
